knitr::opts_hooks$set(engine = function(options) {

## Bin Quality Assessment

I examined instructor-provided CheckM results to evaluate the
completeness and contamination of genome bins recovered from
a black band disease metagenome.

The results were supplied through the MB5370 workshop resources,
rather than generated through a new CheckM run.

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
cd ~/bbd-metagenome
head -n 15 checkm/checkm_results_bbd.txt
```

### Results and Interpretation

Two genome candidates showed particularly high estimated quality:

- `contig_328`: 97.62% completeness and 1.64% contamination.
- `metabat.26`: 97.56% completeness and 0.67% contamination.

Both candidates have high estimated completeness and low
contamination, making them suitable for further investigation.

Other recovered bins showed substantially lower completeness,
highlighting variation in genome recovery quality.

### Selection for Downstream Analysis

I selected genome candidates with estimated completeness
greater than 15% for subsequent taxonomic and functional analysis.

```{bash, eval=FALSE}
cd ~/bbd-metagenome/checkm
awk '$13>15{print $1}' checkm_results_bbd.txt > bbd_topbins.txt
cat bbd_topbins.txt
```

This identified 14 genome candidates for further analysis.
The 15% threshold is an initial screening criterion and
does not mean that every selected genome is high quality.
